newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Petrobras eyes $10 bln in joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Petrobras eyes $10 bln in joint ventures.

text.p: Brazil's state-owned Petrobras and private partners could invest $10 billion in joint ventures following the recent approval of a law opening up the country's oil and gas sectors, Petrobras president Joel Renno said.

"We have signed memoranda with 60 companies and groups. We are going to speed things up as much as possible to sign the partnership contracts this year," Renno said in an interview published in newspaper O Globo Sunday.
"We have 115 projects in production and exploration of petroleum, in refining, ducts and terminals involving investments on the order of $10 billion," Renno said.
A new law, regulating the end of Petrobras' monopoly in the Brazilian petroleum sector, came into effect earlier this month.

The bill allows private companies to compete with Petrobras. But many analysts expect newcomers to be more interested in partnerships with the state-owned giant, which has built up extensive knowledge of Brazil's oil and gas wealth over the last 40 years.
In the Globo interview, Renno also said Petrobras would start operating in the electricity generating sector with its involvement in proposed thermoelectric power plants.
Petrobras would use its share of the power generated by the plants to supply its refineries, Renno said.
